THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 06.03.2026, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1345 OF 2016  2  2026:KER:20341  ORDER

Under challenge in this Revision Petition, at the instance of the complainant, is the judgment dated 23.07.2016 in Crl. Appeal No. 380/2012, passed by the Additional Sessions Court - II,
Thiruvananthapuram, acquitting the accused of the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
2. The 1st respondent herein is the 1st accused in C.C. No. 523/2006, on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court -I, Nedumangad.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court -I, Nedumangad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He along with another accused, stood trial before that court for committing an offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 IPC.

3. The case of the revision petitioner/complainant was that the 1st accused had borrowed an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakhs only) from the complainant on 08.12.2003 and in discharge of the said amount, has issued Ext.P1 post dated cheque dated 08.01.2004 drawn on SBT, Pallithura Branch.
When the cheque was presented for encashment, it returned stating that 'payment stopped by the drawer'.

Thereafter, the complainant after complying with all the statutory requirements,
preferred a complaint under Section CRL.REV.PET NO. 1345 OF 2016 2026:KER:20341 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, as S.T. No. 1557/2004, before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - I, Nedumangad.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - I, Nedumangad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: During the trial, it was revealed that Ext.P1 cheque was issued by the 1 st accused from the account of the 2nd accused.

The complainant, on realising the fact that both accused have purposefully cheated her and thereby, has fraudulently and dishonestly misappropriated an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- from her, approached the trial court by filing C.C. No.
523/2006, alleging commission of an offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 IPC.
4.
During the pendency of C.C. No. 523/2006, the 2 nd accused died and the case against him abated.
But the trial court found the 1st accused guilty of committing an offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 IPC and convicted him thereunder.
It sentenced the 1 st accused to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two years under Section 420 read with Section 34 IPC.

He was further directed to pay a compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- to the complainant, under Section 357(3) of the Cr.P.C.

sentences.text:
The 1st accused carried the matter in appeal by filing CRL.REV.PET NO. 1345 OF 2016 2026:KER:20341 Crl.Appeal No. 380/2012 before the Additional Sessions Court - II,
Thiruvananthapuram.
The said court by judgment dated 23.07.2016, allowed the appeal and acquitted the 1 st accused.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and the learned counsel for the 1st respondent.
7.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioner submitted that the appellate court did not appreciate the evidence on record in a proper perspective and has arrived at a wrong conclusion.
She argued that the accused have obtained Rs.2,00,000/- from the complainant by giving Ext.P1 cheque to her and by representing that it was a cheque issued from the account of the 1st accused.

She submitted that the evidence of PW1 coupled with Exts.P7 to P10 would clearly show that Ext.P1 cheque leaf has been issued in the account of the 2nd accused, and since the signature in Ext.P1 cheque is that of the 1st accused, it can be safely concluded that both the accused had the dishonest intention and at the inception itself, to cheat the complainant and obtain money from her.

8. Per contra, the learned counsel for the 1 st respondent supported the impugned judgment and contended that there are CRL.REV.PET NO. 1345 OF 2016 2026:KER:20341 no grounds to interfere with the same.

He argued that there is no evidence to show that Ext.P1 cheque leaf, in which the signature of the 1st accused finds a place, is not that of the 1 st accused or that it belongs to 2nd accused, as alleged by the complainant.

He also submitted that there is no evidence to show that the accused had a dishonest intention and at the inception itself, in order to attract the offence under Section 420 IPC.
9.
On an anxious consideration of the rival submissions and the materials on record, I find considerable force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the 1 st respondent.
It is the case of the complainant that at the time of borrowing the money, the 1st accused had signed and issued Ext.P1 cheque, which is a cheque leaf issued in the account of the 2 nd accused.
It is also her case that at that time the accused have represented to her that the cheque is of the 1 st accused.

But it is pertinent to note that there is absolutely no evidence to prove that Ext.P1 cheque leaf is one not pertaining to the account of the 1 st accused or that it pertains to the account of the 2 nd accused.

It is true that the revision petitioner is heavily relying upon Ext.P7 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1345 OF 2016 2026:KER:20341 document to substantiate her contention that Ext.P1 cheque leaf pertains to the account of the 2nd accused.
But, it is to be taken note that Ext.P7 has not been proved as required by law, since, the person who has issued it has not been examined.

It is a settled law that mere marking of a document will not amount to proof of its contents, and there is no explanation from the side of the complainant as to why the official concerned, of the bank was not examined to prove Ext.P7.

That apart, it is to be taken note that, the entry in Ext.P7, which is relevant to this case, shows that the name of the person to whom the cheque leaf has been issued is different from the name of the 2 nd accused.

In Ext.P7, the name of the person to whom the cheque leaf is issued is shown as T. V.
Jayan, while the name of the 2nd accused is seen as T. Vijayan.
There is nothing in evidence to show that both these persons are one and the same.

The other documents Exts.P8 and P10, are not of much help to the complainant in substantiating her case, since they only speak about the return of R.Jaya vs Mohanakumaran on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100184139/
3 the cheque.
10.

In these circumstances, I am of the considered view that the appellate court has properly appreciated the evidence CRL.REV.PET NO. 1345 OF 2016 2026:KER:20341 on record and has arrived at a correct conclusion that the 1 st accused is not guilty of the offence alleged.
I do not find any illegality or irregularity in the impugned judgment, warranting the invocation of the revisional jurisdiction from the hands of this Court.
Therefore, I find no merit in this Criminal Revision Petition and the same is accordingly dismissed.
